commonMistakes: Never balance by changing H₂O into H₂O₂; that creates a different substance.

detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).
A chemical formula shows the elements present and the ratio of their atoms. Subscripts belong to the identity of the substance, so changing a subscript changes the substance itself.
Conservation of mass means atoms are not created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. A balanced equation therefore has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides.
Balance equations by changing coefficients in front of formulae, then recount each element. Do not alter subscripts to force the numbers to match.
